purpose: Require semantic fidelity, reproducibility, and visual inspection for any Chapter 5 diagram reconstruction.

items.learning_task: What a student must understand, explain, interpret, or produce
items.diagram_type: uml_class | uml_use_case | uml_activity | uml_sequence | uml_state_machine | uml_component | uml_deployment | dfd | structure_chart | flowchart | concept_model | curve | taxonomy_table

notation.name: exact notation family and version, when relevant
source_defined_conventions: list any conventions stated by the course/source

invariants: testable semantic rule; e.g. exactly seven cohesion types, in source order

code.path: editable source path (.puml, .dot, .mmd, .svg.html, or plot script)
code.renderer: PlantUML | Graphviz DOT | Mermaid | diagram_forge SVG/HTML | Python plotting

validation.visual_review: source and output opened side by side at print scale; legibility result

uml_class: Classes, attributes, operations, relationship kinds, arrowheads, and multiplicities are explicit; subclass generalization points to the superclass.
uml_use_case: Actor-goal associations and system boundary are explicit; include/extend are used only when supported.
uml_activity: Actions, control flows, decisions/merges, guards, and initial/final nodes are typed; do not substitute a generic flowchart.
uml_sequence: Lifelines, message order, activations, returns, and interaction fragments preserve time/order semantics.
uml_state_machine: States, transitions, trigger events, guards, effects, and initial/final pseudostates are typed when present.
uml_component: Implementation components and provided/required interfaces remain distinct from runtime nodes.
uml_deployment: Artifacts/components are mapped to deployment nodes; do not conflate with a component diagram.
dfd: Declare Yourdon/DeMarco or Gane-Sarson; entities, processes, stores, and directed data flows are typed; no call/control-flow arrows; check balancing across levels.
structure_chart: Module hierarchy/calls, data couples, control couples, selection/iteration annotations are distinct; do not reinterpret as DFD or flowchart.
flowchart: Process, input/output, decision, connector, and terminal symbols describe algorithmic control flow.
curve: Axes, units, source-defined qualitative/quantitative scale, sampled points, extrema, and assumptions are recorded; never invent numeric values from a qualitative sketch.
taxonomy_table: Every category and source order are preserved; ranking direction and its legend are explicit.
